A two-layer classifier makes the point: a structural rule (presence of a second funda-mental and of pulses) reaches 94.4% accuracy, whereas the continuous measures alone reach only 0.41–0.55. The call types are three ways of structuring a call, not three frequency bands. For Problem 2, the three correlations are averaged into a fidelity index and fitted with a signal-√ 1 + (d/ds)2γ. Block bootstrap, between-sample ranges and alternative curves quantify the uncertainty. A gated response model fitted to the playbacks shows that a vocal reply requires a fidelity of at most 0.30, while approach requires about 0.49 (95% CI 0.32–0.58). For Problem 3, calls elicit a response in 64.7% of the experiments against 12.9% for the control sound (exact McNemar p = 7.8×10−20). Whether penguins respond depends on context and group size, not on call type. A penalised multinomial model compares calls and control in one framework, and a mixture cure model shows that latency lengthens by a factor of 1.33 per 50 m while 35% of playbacks never elicit a visible response. For Problem 4, an effectiveness index combines tier-specific recognition probabilities with post-recognition behaviour. Contact radii are 155/225/245 m and recruitment radii 83/144/177 m. A 20% loss of correlation shortens the recruitment radius by 21–33%, and a 3 dB rise in noise removes 27–47% of the communication area. Recruitment is lost before contact, which leads to concrete recommendations on vessel noise in foraging areas.

Distance does not affect whether penguins respond but changes how they respond: per 50 m the odds of head-up fall to 0.51 and those of approach to 0.55, while vocal replies do not decline. For approach, mod calls have 3.28 times the odds of flat calls. Variance inflation factors are at most 2.1. The group-size effect has a further implication (Figure 7, right). If each bird responded indepen-dently with a fixed probability, larger groups would respond more often; the opposite is observed. Inverting the independence formula gives 0.3–1.5 expected responders in every size class: about one bird responds per playback, whatever the group size.
